thread:
sam: Quick sync — we're scoping a per-region + per-tier A/B canary flow with model-variant fallbacks. Need decisions on API shape, quota semantics, and console UX. TL;DR: canary across region/tier dims, fall back to compatible variant or lower tier, telemetry must surface fallback reasons. :eyes:
maria: Important: quotas. If a request falls back to a cheaper variant, do we bill the cheaper variant or the original route quota?
lee: +1 on asking that. My vote: bill what actually served (cheaper when cheaper), but keep a headcount of attempted hits to the original variant for exposure metrics.
avani: For rollout scoping — do we model A/B as a single rollout with variant weights, or separate rollout objects per tier/region? I prefer single rollout with multidimensional selectors to avoid duplication.
jamal: Operational concern: a single rollout object with complex selectors makes fallback logic hairy. If a variant isn't available in eu-west-1, router must dynamically resolve to fallback variant and we need clear precedence rules.
lee: API proposal: separate RouterPolicy resource referenced by rollout. RouterPolicy has: selector (region,tier,customer_id patterns), variant_weights, fallback_chain, quota_behavior. That keeps routing decisions decoupled.
sam: That makes sense. But UX needs to keep it simple for customers — they shouldn't have to stitch two objects together for a basic canary. Console should provide templates that wire them up.
ux-kate: Console idea: a 2D matrix UI (region x tier). Each cell shows percent exposure and a dropdown of variants. Default quickflow: pick region(s) -> pick tier(s) -> set weights. Advanced: "link RouterPolicy" for shared rules. :sparkles:
maria: On quota_behavior we need explicit options: "charge_served", "charge_requested", "charge_original_with_override". Each has billing implications and legal/contract impact for Dedicated customers.
avani: Telemetry: require these tags on each server-side event: route_policy_id, rollout_id, variant_id, fallback_reason (enum), original_target_variant. That lets us attribute quality/regression to attempts vs. actual serves.
telemetry-bot: Added schema v2.3: tags=["route_policy_id","rollout_id","variant_id","fallback_reason","region","tier"] — will start backfilling for new rollouts.
jamal: Fallback precedence brainstorming: 1) explicit variant in same rollout, 2) compatible model catalog variant (quantized/CPU), 3) lower-tier approved variant, 4) regional proxy to other region (if allowed by policy), 5) failover error. We need a config flag for cross-region fallback opt-in.
lee: Edge case: customer pins a version and tier=enterprise. If we fallback to lower tier variant, are we violating SLA? Need contract gating and an "allow_tier_downgrade" boolean per rollout.
maria: Also need quota accounting visibility in Console: show attempted vs served tokens per cell. Customers will ask why their enterprise quota dropped but they saw cheaper variant serves.
sam: UX for alerts: canary health alerts should trigger on both served-metrics and attempted-metrics. Example: model v2 served latency ok but attempted->v2 error rate high -> means routing failing before serve.
ux-kate: For the matrix UI we can surface small icons: ⚠️ for attempted>served delta, 💸 for billing mismatch (if charge_requested), 📉 for quality regressions. Hover shows recent events.
lee: Quick API sketch (pseudo-JSON):
```
{
  "router_policy_id": "rp-123",
  "selector": {"regions": ["eu-west-1","us-east-1"], "tiers": ["enterprise"]},
  "variants": [{"id":"v2","weight":80},{"id":"v2-quant","weight":20}],
  "fallback_chain": ["v2-quant","v1-compat","lower-tier-v2"],
  "quota_behavior": "charge_served",
  "allow_tier_downgrade": false
}
```
avani: Love that. For A/B we just adjust weights. For per-tenant scoping we allow overlays (tenant-specific policy overrides). Overlay should be last-mile and small to avoid explosion.
jamal: Runtime concern: router must evaluate availability quickly. Caching node-level capability (which variants present on that pool/region) will be mandatory. Need invalidation TTL and a fast fallback path.
deploy-bot: deploy succeeded for routing-cache-update :thumbsup: (2024-11-03T14:02:10Z)
sam: Action items: 1) Lee + Maria to draft RouterPolicy proto and quota enums, 2) Avani + UX to prototype matrix flow + "quick create" template, 3) Jamal to spec runtime capability cache & TTL, 4) Telemetry team to ensure fallback_reason tagging.
telemetry-bot: Noted. Will create a dashboard template: "rollout / fallback heatmap" with attempted vs served, fallback reasons breakdown.
ux-kate: I'll mock the matrix screens and a fallback heatmap widget by EOD Friday.
maria: I'll draft billing note for charge behaviors and get legal eyes for Dedicated contracts.
sam: Great. If nobody objects, we'll move RouterPolicy as a first-class resource and make Console provide the simple wiring. If we hit complexity, fallback to "one-rollout-per-scope" fallback. :+1:
lee: No objections from me.
avani: fine by me.
jamal: good to go.
sam: Thanks everyone. Closing thread unless someone raises a blocker. :lock:
